title: Why Testing AI on Aged Leads First Sets It Up to Fail
summary: Testing voice AI on aged leads feels safe, but it hides AI’s biggest advantage: speed. Here’s why remodelers should pilot on real-time leads instead.
body_markdown:
By[Pam Torrey](https://www.linkedin.com/in/pam-torrey-920175b4/) , Senior Director of Marketing at Leaping AI


“Let’s try it on our old leads first.”


When most remodelers gear up to test voice AI in their businesses, that’s the first thing they’ll say. If the AI makes a mistake or isn’t quite right from the jump, you haven’t burned a fresh lead the marketing team paid for. If it books a few appointments, that’s gravy.


But this test isn’t measuring the right thing.


Aged leads are a challenge for everyone, including your best call center rep. And they take away the one thing voice AI does better than any inside sales team: reaching every lead the moment it comes in.


So, the AI voice agent books fewer appointments than you had hoped and the conclusion becomes, “AI doesn’t work for us.” Which is the wrong conclusion from a test that was never fair to begin with. (We make the full case for starting with fresh leads in[Should Remodelers Use Voice AI on Real-Time Leads or Aged Leads?](https://leapingai.com/blog/voice-ai-real-time-vs-aged-leads) )


## **A two-week-old lead has already made other plans**


The research on lead response has said the same thing for more than a decade. A lead’s value drops in minutes, not weeks.


The[Lead Response Management Study](https://www.electronics-cooling.com/2011/06/increase-your-sales-effectiveness-by-21x-in-25-minutes/) from MIT’s James Oldroyd and InsideSales.com found the odds of reaching a lead were 100 times higher when you called within five minutes instead of 30. The odds of qualifying that lead were 21 times higher.


Things get worse when a company waits even an hour to get back to a lead. In[“The Short Life of Online Sales Leads,”](https://hbr.org/2011/03/the-short-life-of-online-sales-leads) Harvard Business Review reported that companies that reached out within an hour were nearly seven times as likely to qualify a lead as those that waited longer. When you compare that to companies that waited a day or more, they were more than 60 times as likely.


Let’s apply this to a hypothetical scenario. Imagine a lead from two weeks ago. The homeowner filled out a form on Angi to get quotes on an upcoming project. Since then, they have been called by three other companies who bought the same lead. They booked two appointments for an in-home consultation and have quotes with financing options from both. At this point, they’re going to decide between the two companies they met and are likely not answering unknown numbers anymore.


That’s the lead you’re asking AI to win with this test.


## **Speed is AI’s edge, and aged leads erase it**


Home services companies are not known for fast follow-up. In a[2018 secret-shopper test of 466 home services companies](https://conxpros.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/12/Speed2Lead-case-study.pdf) , Valve+Meter found 95% didn’t respond in under five minutes and 55% didn’t respond within a day. Forty percent never responded at all, and 85% never called a second time.


Voice AI doesn’t have that problem. With Leaping AI’s Campaigns, you can reach out to a lead the moment it comes in and follow up by call and text until you reach them. It works the same at 9 p.m. on a Saturday as it does at 10 a.m. on a Tuesday, giving homeowners the same experience regardless of when they have time to shop.


On a brand-new lead, that puts you first in line while most companies are still checking their inboxes.


On a two-week-old lead there isn’t any line left to be first in. The AI is calling a cold list that was already worked by your CSRs, and the results will look like any reactivation campaign. Connect and conversion rates will be lower than on fresh leads. It is still worth contacting those leads, but it shouldn’t be the bar by which you measure voice AI.


## **What happened when one remodeler ran the aged-lead test**


We recently worked with a window and siding company that implemented Leaping AI on leads that were about two weeks old and waited to see what was booked. It booked fewer appointments than they wanted. Many teams would have stopped right there and said there was a problem with the technology.


Instead, the Leaping AI team showed their leadership how Campaigns would work on a new lead: the instant text, the immediate calls, the follow-up that continues after those first attempts. Once they saw that, they agreed to do a two-month test on real-time leads, tracking the AI agent’s conversion rate.


On real-time leads, the AI agent’s appointments held up better than the in-house team’s. Fewer of them dropped (30% vs. 42%), fewer sales canceled before the job was issued (11% vs. 20%), and each appointment brought in about 7% more revenue. The company has since increased its investment with Leaping AI by 3.4x.


## **How to run a test that’s fair to AI and to your team**


If you want to test voice AI in your company to see how it will set appointments, focus on where speed matters most. A fair pilot of the technology has four parts:


1.


**Use real-time leads.** Send new leads to the AI as they come in, so it can respond in seconds.


2.


**Set a timeframe.** Run long enough to cover evenings, weekends, and normal swings in lead volume. Six to eight weeks is a good place to start, depending on your lead volume.


3.


**Follow up more than once.** One call isn’t follow-up. Campaigns can run 100 touchpoints over 30 days across calls and texts, so a homeowner who doesn’t answer today still hears from you next week.


4.


**Track the same numbers.** Measure appointments set, shown, and sold together, using the same definitions you use for your reps.


## **Where aged leads still fit**


Older leads are worth working. Reactivating them is a smart step once AI is handling new leads and you trust the results.


Those leads just shouldn’t be the test that decides whether AI belongs in your call center.
